All major target field categories are covered by identified source candidates: (a) disease/country/subnational_location — all sources; (b) locality — VBDS Annual Report 2024 (county-level table), glamosquito.org (neighborhood-level LA data with August 2024 dates); (c) date_reported — CDPH NR24-27 (2024 season), contracosta.news (2024-10-01 dateline), glamosquito.org (specific August dates); (d) cases_confirmed/cases_probable/cases_unspecified — CDPH VBDS Annual Report 2024 (county breakdown), CDPH year-end monthly PDF (type breakdown: neuroinvasive 103, non-neuroinvasive 30, asymptomatic 20); (e) deaths — CDPH NR24-27 (6 deaths), CDPH year-end total (153 cases); (f) hospitalizations — partially covered (CDPH sources may include this; not confirmed in snippets); (g) source_url/source_type/evidence_quote — multiple sources with quotable snippets. iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: HIGH. The dominant sources are official California state government agencies: CDPH (cdph.ca.gov) and the California WNV surveillance portal (westnile.ca.gov), both operated by CDPH/CDFA. The CDPH VBDS Annual Report 2024 is the gold-standard annual surveillance document. The CDC ArboNET historic data page provides federal-level cross-validation. County-level sources (kernpublichealth.com, ruhealth.org, nevadacountyca.gov, glamosquito.org) are official or quasi-official local public health entities. The contracosta.news article is a secondary source but explicitly republishes CDPH figures. The s47353.pcdn.co PDF is a 2023 document and should be deprioritized. Facebook results should be excluded. No peer-reviewed literature was surfaced, which is expected for a one-month 2024 window.
